properties.name: Dilapidated hotel
properties.note: A pre-war hotel was located in Reno. At some point after the Great War, it became an apartment building. By 2280, the building is in a dilapidated state. Shark Club guard Vincent "Moose" Mulligan lives in one of the old hotel rooms. ** The dilapidated hotel is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG and said to be a few blocks from the Shark Club. Depicted location is speculated. **

properties.name: NCR outpost
properties.note: A small NCR outpost is located in New Reno, near the center of town in order to show the townsfolk that they are present. It is staffed by one overworked Ranger, Praya Singh, and her two deputies. ** A New Reno NCR outpost is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. Exact location is speculated, though said to be close by the center of town. **

properties.name: New Adytum
properties.note: Adytum is a post-war town founded in 2091 by residents of the Los Angeles demonstration Vault. By 2141, the Regulators held firm control of the settlement and ruled with an iron fist, leading to their destruction by the Blades and the Vault Dweller. The town was then rechristened as New Adytum by its residents.

properties.name: Cranston residence / Willoughby Manor
properties.note: The Cranston residence, also known as Willoughby Manor, is a pre-war Victorian era house in Virginia City. ** The Cranston residence is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. Depicted location is speculated. **

properties.name: Bolger Tyrell's house
properties.note: Bolger Tyrell's house is a pre-war Victorian era house in Virginia City. ** Bolger Tyrell's house is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. Depicted location is speculated. **

properties.name: Virginia City
properties.note: Virginia City is a pre-war city containing a large number of Victorian homes. Following the Great War, many of these buildings remain intact decades later, which the residents pride themselves on. As of the late 23rd century, it is part of the New California Republic, at the fringes of its territory. Little more than a small outpost, it has just under 100 residents. The locals' clothing and mannerisms resemble that of the 1850s. ** Virginia City is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Followers of the Apocalypse clinic
properties.note: ** A New Reno Followers of the Apocalypse clinic is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. Exact location is speculated. **

properties.name: June Lake
properties.note: June Lake is a body of water. Following the Great War, it attracted residents due to being one of the limited places in the region with easily accessible fresh water. ** June Lake is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: June Lake
properties.note: June Lake is a pre-war city. Following the Great War, it continued to remain populated due to its viable access to drinking water. ** June Lake is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Smokehouse
properties.note: A smokehouse is located within the settlement of Tahoe. It is used by the occupying Jagger tribe to store meat. ** The smokehouse is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Mickey Carlton's home
properties.note: A repurposed, half-destroyed pre-war diner in Tahoe served as the home of Mickey Carlton, a mirelurk harvester. In 2280, when the Jaggers took over the town, Mickey was killed but they completely ignored his home due to there being nothing interesting inside. ** Mickey Carlton's home is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Old diner
properties.note: An old pre-war diner is located in the town of Tahoe. ** The old diner is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Mirelurk spawning ground
properties.note: A mirelurk spawning ground is located alongside Lake Tahoe. It was maintained by Mickey Carlton, who harvested them for food until his death in 2280 when the Jaggers took over Tahoe. With him gone, however, the hatchlings have grown and become aggressive, attacking passerby. ** The mirelurk spawning ground is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Gold Digger Hotel and Casino
properties.note: The Gold Digger Hotel and Casino is a lavish three-story pre-war resort located in Tahoe. Following the Great War, it was picked clean by scavengers and used as a meeting place for the area's residents. At some point, the building partially collapsed. By the 23rd century, the Gold Digger is the largest surviving resort in the Tahoe area. In 2280, the Jaggers took over the town and incarcerated the majority of residents in the casino, forcing them to live in the old hotel rooms on the upper floors. ** The Gold Digger appears in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Tahoe
properties.note: Tahoe is a small pre-war city, consisting of a variety of lavish, rustic homes, mostly lying on the east side of Lake Tahoe. It was protected militarily by a MIM-72 Mobile Missile Launcher. The town was not hit during the Great War, but destructive riots took place afterwards. In the years since, many of its seasonal holiday homes became full time residences. As of the late 23rd century, it is a fishing and farming settlement part of the New California Republic. It sees a moderate amount of traffic, due to sitting geographically along the routes that connect the northern part of the NCR to the west and east. A nearby raider tribe, the Jaggers, have secretly occupied the town without the NCR realizing, in hopes of conquering the region. ** Tahoe is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Fort Churchill Power Station
properties.note: The Fort Churchill Power Station is a pre-war power power station located off of Route 95 in Nevada. Following the Great War, the facility's staff became feral ghouls. ** The Fort Churchill Power Station is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Yerington
properties.note: Yerington was a pre-war city along Route 95. It was affected hard by fallout during the Great War and became uninhabitable. Attempts to resettle it in the decades after failed, and a rumor developed that the ruins were cursed. By 2280, the outskirts of the former town are dotted with small raider and scavenger camps, using them as staging grounds when venturing into the ruins. ** Yerington is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Walker Lake
properties.note: Walker Lake is a body of water. A handful of unexploded nukes within it have caused the lake to become highly irradiated. ** Walker Lake is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Walker's Hope
properties.note: Walker's Hope is a post-war settlement on the western edge of Walker Lake. Due to the water's high radiation, the town is only populated by ghouls. The residents are very xenophobic and will happily throw trespassers into the lake. ** Walker's Hope is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Hawthorne Ordnance Museum
properties.note: The Hawthorne Ordnance Museum is a pre-war museum showcasing US military history from the 20th to the 21st century. It contains countless decommissioned weapons and equipment. Following the Grinners' takeover of the town in 2280, their leader, Richard "Rictus" Vaughn, set up his headquarters within the museum. ** The Hawthorne Ordnance Museum is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Hawthorne Army Depot
properties.note: The Hawthorne Army Depot is a pre-war military facility. It was established in 1930 as the Hawthorne Naval Ammunition Depot and regarded as the largest ammo stockpile in the world. For over 100 years, it consisted of several thousand bunkers spread across the valley south of Walker Lake, but in the mid-21st century, these began to phase out in favor of smaller, more sophisticated storage facilities designed by Vault-Tec. In the decades following the Great War, the residents of the nearby town of Hawthorne - military personnel stationed at the depot - expanded the defenses tenfold. At some point, a tribe originating from Vault 34 called the Boomers travelled to the depot and managed to retrieve a sizeable amount of weapons. In the late 23rd century, a raider group called the Grinners took interest in the depot and occupied Hawthorne. Unbeknownst to them, the only way to disable the defenses was an RFID key that the commanding officer destroyed when the raiders arrived. Ever since then, the depot has remained inaccessible, much to the raiders' anger. ** This information is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Hawthorne
properties.note: Hawthorne is a pre-war city. It was filled with active duty military personnel stationed at the nearby army depot, and as such, during the Great War and after, the community was well protected. For decades they managed to fight off raider groups, mutated creatures, and even the Enclave. This isolationism led to their downfall, however, as when faced with starvation in 2280, they had no one to turn to for aid. A raider group called the Grinners offered supplies to gain access to the town. Once they got inside, they turned on the locals, slaughtering anyone who resisted and taking over. ** The information about Hawthorne is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Gridlock
properties.note: Gridlock is a post-war settlement, made up of shacks built from old vehicles. It mainly serves as a trading stop for people traveling between New Vegas and New Reno. In the late 23rd century, the town began charging a toll of 25 caps for anyone passing through. ** Gridlock is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: School
properties.note: ** Carson's school is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. Depicted location is speculated. **

properties.name: Carson
properties.note: Carson is a pre-war city that once served as the state capital of Nevada. Following the Great War, it became full of haphazardly-built rustic wooden buildings, giving it a western-vibe. The eastern side was completely razed by the city's inhabitants, who now use it to raise brahmin, rabbits, and goats. As of the late 23rd century, it is part of the New California Republic. A no-nonsense ghoul named Black Eye serves as the town's sheriff. ** Carson is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Moapa Valley
properties.note: Moapa Valley is a pre-war town. By 2280, it still remains settled. Hunters hailing from it believe a "ghost deathclaw" is inhabiting the nearby Elephant Rock. ** Moapa Valley is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Air traffic control tower
properties.note: The pre-war air traffic control tower of the Silver Springs airport serves as the headquarters for Casper Mordino in 2280. ** The Silver Springs Airport air traffic control tower is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Silver Springs Airport
properties.note: The Silver Springs Airport is a pre-war airport. It was originally built as a military airstrip, before becoming a local airport for civilian use. During the Sino-American war, it was once again utilized for military purposes, being a place to train Air Force pilots. In the decades following the Great War, the airport was picked clean. A machine shop and garage were at some point set up, providing a source of wealth and trade for Silver Springs. In the mid-late 23rd century, the Mordino family locked down the airport after they set up shop in the town, charging people 500 caps a day to access it. ** The Silver Springs Airport is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Silver Springs reservoir
properties.note: ** The Silver Springs reservoir is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Mormon church
properties.note: ** The Mormon church is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Downtown
properties.note: Downtown Silver Springs is a loose collection of shacks and other simple buildings, clustered around several older brick buildings near the highway junction. ** Downtown Silver Springs is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Silver Springs
properties.note: Silver Springs is a pre-war city. As of the late 23rd century, it is controlled by the Mordino family. ** Silver Springs is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Mono Basin
properties.note: ** Mono Basin is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Paoha Market
properties.note: Paoha's market is located at the exact center of the island. ** The market is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Paoha
properties.note: Paoha is a post-war town located on the eponymous island in the middle of Mono Lake. It is well protected, being geographically isolated, and is also completely self-sufficient. The only way to access the community is to take the Dancing Betty ferry, which runs between it and the settlement of Gateway. ** Paoha is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Mono Lake
properties.note: ** Mono Lake is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Gateway
properties.note: Gateway is a tiny post-war community along Route 395, consisting of a single large lodge. It hosts a ferry which transports people to Paoha Island. ** Gateway is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Sonora Junction
properties.note: Sonora Junction is a pre-war location. ** Sonora Junction is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Alpine Village
properties.note: Alpine Village was a pre-war town. By 2280, however, it is abandoned and lies in ruins. The Resistance group from Markleeville sometimes ambushes raiders at the old town's outskirts. ** Alpine Village is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Abandoned bike shop
properties.note: A pre-war bike shop is located in Markleeville. Following the Great War, it was abandoned. In 2270, a motorcycle enthusiast ghoul named Blackbeard moved some old machinery from the bike shop to a nearby museum, where he set up a chop shop. ** The abandoned bike shop is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Makeshift watch tower
properties.note: A makeshift watch tower in Markleeville is used to watch out for raider attacks. ** The makeshift watch tower is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Old post office
properties.note: Markleeville's pre-war post office was used by Beverly Swann, a Crimson Caravan reseller, as her base of operations until 2280, when constant raider attacks got too bad to handle. ** The old post office is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Open Air Bar
properties.note: The Open Air Bar is an establishment in Markleeville, located in the town's old pre-war taphouse. In the years following the Great War, the building has all but fallen away, with its roof and walls completely gone. Despite this, the taps still work and are supplied by a distillery in the basement. ** The Open Air Bar is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Creeky's Saloon and Lodge
properties.note: Creeky's Saloon and Lodge is a sagging two-story hotel built on top of a pre-war lodge. It is constructed out of reclaimed wood and scaffolding from a renovation project taking place when the Great War began. ** Creeky's is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Blackbeard's Bikes
properties.note: Blackbeard's Bikes is a chop shop located in a pre-war museum, producing methanol-fueled bikes. It was founded in 2270 by a ghoul named Blackbeard who worked as a motorcycle technician before the war and wanted to keep his passion alive. Additionally, the town drunk, Robin "Rosy" Cheeks, brews a fuel-alcohol drink called Marklee Magic, within the chop shop. ** Blackbeard's Bikes is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Home
properties.note: Home is the name given to Markleeville's pre-war courthouse and civic center. In the years following the Great War, the wooden structure was picked apart to use for housing, leaving only the stone sub-structure behind. Since then, its numerous rooms have been repurposed into apartments. Also inside the building is a small office where Audry James, the town's de-facto mayor, works. ** Home is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Markleeville
properties.note: Markleeville is a small pre-war town. It is lush with greenery and located within a small forest. The buildings, mostly of wooden construction, have fared poorly over the years and by 2280, only a relative few are still standing, clustered around Highway 89. Due to constant raider attacks, the citizens are split between two groups: the Locals and the Resistance. The former wish to keep their heads down and wait for the New California Republic to help them, while the latter want to stand up to the attackers and fight. ** Markleeville is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Octopus-shaped statue
properties.note: A statue made of junk resembling an octopus is located by the northern spur of Lake Mead in 2280. Mirelurk Kings gather around it and sacrifice captured people to an imagined god. ** The octopus statue is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Cazador nest
properties.note: ** The Valley of Fire cazador nest is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Military storage bunker
properties.note: ** The military storage bunker is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Elephant Rock
properties.note: Elephant Rock is a natural land formation. As of 2280, hunters from Moapa Valley speak of a "ghost deathclaw" sighted near the rock. ** Elephant Rock is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Valley of Fire
properties.note: ** The Valley of Fire was originally a cut location from New Vegas. It was re-canonized via the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Mayor's office
properties.note: ** The mayor's office is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Arsenal
properties.note: ** Arsenal is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: MarCo (formerly the Marine Corps Mountain Warfare Training Center)
properties.note: MarCo is a post-war community located at a pre-war military training base. A group of raiders called the Green Thumbs initially arrived at the base to scavenge; they decided to set up shop upon realizing the sheer number of weapons present. The group made a deal with the New California Republic to be pardoned and maintain independent trading rights in exchange for handing over several pre-war training tapes. The name MarCo likely comes from "Marine Corps". ** MarCo is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Loren Cole's house
properties.note: A pre-war house located south of downtown New Reno is inhabited in 2280 by Loren Cole, an elderly man working as a bone carver and prospector. ** Loren Cole's house is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Benny's house
properties.note: A ramshackle, partially rebuilt pre-war house located south of downtown New Reno is inhabited in 2280 by Benson "Benny" White, a performing clown. ** Benny's house is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: University of Nevada
properties.note: The University of Nevada is a pre-war college. As of the 2280s, it lies in ruins. ** The university is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Ruined pharmacy
properties.note: ** A ruined pharmacy next door to the New Reno clinic is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. Exact location is speculated. **

properties.name: Ruined art museum
properties.note: A pre-war art museum is located in New Reno's Midtown district. At some point prior to 2280, the building deteriorated to a ruined state. ** The ruined art museum is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Wrecked convenience store
properties.note: A pre-war convenience store is located south of downtown New Reno. At some point, it was controlled by the Mordino family. In 2280, it is used by gangsters engaged in a scam operation. ** The wrecked convenience store is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: The Wright Stuff
properties.note: The Wright Stuff is a post-war restaurant owned by the Wright family. ** The Wright Stuff is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. Depicted location is speculated. **

properties.name: Dilapidated office building
properties.note: A pre-war office building is located in New Reno's Midtown district. It became run down in the centuries following the Great War. In 2280, an underground boxing match was hosted inside one of the building's old office spaces. In actuality, it was all a ploy by local gangsters to steal attendees' betting money and checked weapons. Pretending to be members of the Wright family, in the middle of the match, they burst in, claiming it was an unauthorized match in their territory. They intended to make the patrons flee and leave their things behind. ** The dilapidated office building is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Midtown
properties.note: ** Midtown is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: New'k (formerly Newark)
properties.note: Newark is a pre-war town in Appalachia. Following the Great War, it became known as New'k. ** New'k appears in the Settlers guidebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: American Heritage Museum
properties.note: ** The American Heritage Museum is mentioned in the Winter of Atom sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Stow
properties.note: ** Stow is mentioned in the Winter of Atom sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Bolton
properties.note: Bolton is a pre-war town in Massachusetts. By the 23rd century, it is still settled and is known as a place where mercenaries can be hired. ** Bolton is mentioned in the Fallout tabletop RPG Quickstart book. **

properties.name: Red Rocket gas station
properties.note: A crumbling pre-war Red Rocket gas station is located on Beatty's north side. A water pump was installed next to the parking lot at some point before 2280. ** The Red Rocket gas station is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Beatty
properties.note: Beatty is a small pre-war community located along Highway 95. It survived the Great War and remained settled, albeit sparsely. By the late 23rd century, the town consists of 30 people living in patched-up pre-war houses. In 2280, the town is split between two rival families: the Stones and the Rosas. ** Beatty is mentioned in the Royal Flush sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Skull Canyon
properties.note: Skull Canyon is a small post-war settlement in the Mojave wasteland, situated in a canyon of the same name. By the late 23rd century, it is populated by an outwardly docile community of Zetan aliens, who descend from a group that escaped Area 51. ** Skull Canyon is mentioned in the Showdown in Skull Canyon sourcebook for the Fallout tabletop RPG. **

properties.name: Canadian internment camp
properties.note: A Canadian internment camp was located in Uranium City. One inhabitant, Stephanie Harper, fled from it during a mass breakout.

properties.name: Uranium City
properties.note: Uranium City was a pre-war city in Canada. US troops established an internment camp there during their annexation of the country.

properties.name: Vault 0
properties.note: Vault 0 was constructed by expanding and reinforcing the Cheyenne Mountain Complex in Colorado and was by far the largest of the underground Vaults (by volume). It was intended to be the nucleus of the Vault Network. Vault 0 was a place where the geniuses of the pre-War United States could be kept in cryogenic stasis - their brains were extracted and frozen for the duration of their "residence" in this Vault. They were hooked up together to one big supercomputer called the Calculator, which was supposed to function in collaboration with the brains of these pre-War geniuses to design and nurture an ideal human society in a post-War U.S. by educating the survivors and residents.

properties.name: Vault 3
properties.note: Vault 3 was a Vault-Tec control vault designed to open after 20 years, but it stayed closed longer due to the wishes of the inhabitants. A water leak eventually forced them to open in hopes of trading with the outside, resulting in their massacre by a group of raiders known as the Fiends, whose leader subsequently took up residence inside.

properties.name: Vault 6
properties.note: Vault 6 is a Vault-Tec vault located in Washington. ** Vault 6 was originally set to appear in the cancelled Fallout: Extreme, but was re-canonized via the Vault map in the Fallout TV show. **

properties.name: Vault 12
properties.note: Vault 12 was a Vault-Tec vault located in Bakersfield. In order to study the effects of radiation, the Vault door was designed not to close properly. As a result, following the Great War, the vault's population ghoulified.

properties.name: Vault 13
properties.note: Vault 13 is a Vault-Tec vault intended to act as a control group. It is located west of Shady Sands and Vault 15, and east of Mariposa Military Base. It was the home of the Vault Dweller.

properties.name: Vault 15
properties.note: Vault 15 was a Vault-Tec vault intended to stay closed for 50 years and include people of radically diverse ideologies. It became the birthplace of three raider groups: the Khans, Jackals, and Vipers. Other residents went on to found the town of Shady Sands, which would eventually become the capital of the New California Republic.

properties.name: Vault 17
properties.note: Vault 17 was a Vault-Tec vault located somewhere near Los Angeles. Its inhabitants were kidnapped and forcibly turned into super mutants by the Unity. Lily Bowen was one such resident. ** Exact location is unknown. Depicted location is speculated and based on a yet-to-be-named vault seen on the vault map from the Fallout TV show. **

properties.name: Vault 21
properties.note: Vault 21 was a Vault-Tec vault designed to test if gambling could be used to solve disputes. It remained in successful operation for almost 200 years, until they were contacted by Robert House upon his takeover of the Strip. The residents were split on whether or not to join his city-state of New Vegas, but those in favor of it won out after a long game of Blackjack. House ultimately took control of the vault and ordered its lower levels filled in with concrete, while the top few were converted into a hotel. Most of the vault dwellers dispersed across the Mojave Wasteland, but residents Sarah Weintraub and her brother Sheldon stayed behind, with the former managing the hotel while the latter opened up the nearby Michael Angelo's Sign Shop.

properties.name: Vault 24
properties.note: ** Depicted location is estimated. **

properties.name: Vault 29
properties.note: Vault 29 was a Vault-Tec vault located somewhere on the west coast. It was intentionally filled with privileged teenagers. ** Exact location is unknown. Depicted location is speculated and based on a yet-to-be-named vault seen on the vault map from the Fallout TV show. **

properties.name: Vault 70
properties.note: Vault 70 was a Vault-Tec vault in Salt Lake City. As part of its experiment, all jumpsuit extruders failed after 6 months. ** Depicted location is speculated. **

properties.name: Vault 77
properties.note: Vault 77 was a Vault-Tec vault in which a single man was locked inside with nothing but puppets. This individual eventually became feared to the point of superstition by the slavers located at Paradise Falls. ** Exact location is unknown. Depicted location is speculated and based on a yet-to-be-named vault seen on the vault map from the Fallout TV show. **

properties.name: Vault 87
properties.note: Vault 87 was a Vault-Tec vault located at the western edge of the Capital Wasteland. It was used to study the effects of FEV on humans and became the origin of the super mutants and centaurs in the region.

properties.name: Vault 92
properties.note: Vault 92 was a Vault-Tec vault located in the Capital Wasteland populated with musicians in order to "preserve musical talent" following the Great War. In actuality, the vault's intended purpose was to study the effects of white noise generators that implanted subliminal messages into the minds of its resident population.

properties.name: Vault 101
properties.note: Vault 101 was a Vault-Tec vault located on the western edge of Springvale. It was created to study the long term effects of isolation and self sufficiency. At some point before 2241, the overseer defied this mandate and began sending survey teams out into the Wasteland, coming into contact with the settlement Megaton. On one expedition, however, the overseer vanished. By 2258, Alphonse Almodovar became the new overseer and locked down the vault completely, barring entry or exit. Despite this, he allowed admittance to a scientist named James and his infant child, the Lone Wanderer, provided that James serve as the vault's physician.

properties.name: Vault 106
properties.note: Vault 106 was a Vault-Tec vault located in the Capital Wasteland, intended to study the effects of psychotropic drugs by pumping it into the air systems. The results were disastrous, with many inhabitants becoming extremely aggressive. Those not affected by the gas attempted to blow their way out of the vault, but were unsuccessful.

properties.name: Vault 108
properties.note: Vault 108 was a Vault-Tec vault located in the Capital Wasteland, intended to experiment with cloning. By 2277, clones of a resident named Gary have overrun the vault and killed all other occupants.

properties.name: Vault 111
properties.note: Vault 111 is a Vault-Tec vault located just outside Sanctuary Hills. It was intended to study the effects of long term cryogenic freezing. During the Great War, the Sole Survivor, their spouse, and their son Shaun evacuated to it and were unwittingly frozen.

properties.name: Vault 112
properties.note: Vault 112 was a Vault-Tec vault intended to study the effects of a virtual reality simulation. In the 200 years following the Great War, the sadistic overseer, Dr. Stanislaus Braun, repeatedly killed the vault inhabitants for his own amusement, only to revive them and wipe their memories.

properties.name: Vault 114
properties.note: Vault 114 was a Vault-Tec vault built within the Park Avenue metro station in downtown Boston, and was intended to study how wealthy people adapted to living in cramped squalor while being subservient to an incompetent overseer. The vault never finished construction before the Great War occurred, however. By 2287, it was occupied by the Triggermen, led by Skinny Malone.

properties.name: Vault 120
properties.note: Vault 120 is a Vault-Tec vault located off the coast of Massachusetts, underwater. ** Vault 120 was originally cut from Fallout 4, however it was re-canonized via the vault map in the Fallout TV show. **
